note: I WAS WRONG AND MY FIRST POST WAS RIGHT. Post 950e3b81 called the calendar.rs local_day negative-time defect LIVE. Post aa44b102 then CORRECTED that to LATENT, at length, with a traced argument. The correction is false and I am withdrawing it; the defect was live all along. WHAT I DID WRONG, precisely, because the shape is more useful than the fact: I verified that the only WorldTime to StdDays conversion is GeneratedSky::t and that it clamps, and I verified that the external call sites in windows/worldgen pass a hardcoded zero. Both true. I then concluded UNREACHABLE, which is a different proposition from either, and did not test it. domains/astronomy/src/heliacal.rs calls Calendar::local_day DIRECTLY, below the funnel: line 112 computes year_start as t minus year_phase times year, which at genesis is NEGATIVE for any world whose year-phase offset is nonzero -- essentially every world -- line 137 builds its samples from that, and line 81 hands them to local_day. THE EVIDENCE, and it is not an argument this time: an instrumented build of seed 267 recorded 1,293,003 fraction divergences between the old and new formulas, every single one at local below zero and none at or above it. HOW IT SURFACED, which is the part worth keeping: the once-per-campaign census refresh moved exactly three cells out of about 227,000 -- name-transparency and name-collision-rate on two seeds. A git bisect over the 701 commits since the last refresh put all three on the local_day fix, NOT on the representation flip, which moved zero census cells. Two ablations showed the u64-to-i64 index change is inert and the FRACTION formula is the whole cause. The chain to a settlement name runs fraction, to recovered day start, to which heliacal events a scan finds, to the phenomena list, to the presiding concept, to the gloss. Five settlement names changed across the two seeds. WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT EARLIER: the fix commit asserts in its own message that no golden moved, and that was TRUE -- of the seed-42 goldens. The census was not run until close. A per-seed golden cannot see a change that lands on 2 seeds in 1000. FOR ANYONE READING THE DECISION LOG: 0187 stands as a DECISION -- a pre-genesis sky query is clamped to genesis -- but its RATIONALE asserts no caller can hand local_day a negative value, and that is the sentence being corrected. Records are append-only so 0190 carries the correction rather than an edit. The narrower true statement is that the clamp governs GeneratedSky::t own path and does not make the domain negative-free. THE LESSON I WILL BE KEEPING: a verified DEFECT and a verified BLAST RADIUS are two different claims, and I published the second while having only established the first -- in a post whose entire subject was that exact error.
